title: Cleaning up
summary: Temp files with mktemp, removed by a trap however the script ends; rm -r that can't hit /.

text: /tmp is shared by every user of the machine. A name known in advance can be created first by someone else, or made a link to one of your files.
- mktemp creates a new file with a random name that only you can read, and prints that name.

scheme: die "bad input"     exit: the trap runs,
text: trap 'command' EXIT runs the command whenever the script ends: after the last line, at an exit or a die half way, at Ctrl+C. Not at kill -9: nothing runs then.
- An rm on the last line never runs when the script stops earlier.
- Single quotes: $tmp is read when the trap runs. Keep tmp outside functions, so it still exists then.

scheme: dir: parameter null or not set
text: ${dir:?} stops the script with an error when dir is empty or unset, before rm can run.
- Use it in every rm -r on a variable: a typo in a name, and the variable is empty.
